LanguageData.CC_SetSec_Direction_Note: One of Rimfolk's eight ways to play, leaning whichever storyteller you play. With one of the eight as your storyteller, it plays its own way unless a direction is chosen here.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_StoryDirection_Tip: Leans the storyteller you play toward one of Rimfolk's eight ways to play. It shapes Rimfolk's own happenings (visitors, camps, letters, favours, missions, world situations, friends in a fight) and who a raid comes from. The storyteller keeps its own pace of threats and sickness. It leans toward something, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come. It can be changed at any time, in a running game too.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection: Leans any storyteller toward one of the eight ways to play.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_None: No lean: the storyteller plays as it does (one of the eight plays its own way).
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_LongRoad: More letters, favours asked, camps, missions and word from the region.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_Neighbours: Raids mostly come from a people with a reason; more visitors, letters, favours and friends.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_TurningYear: Camps, trade, visitors, letters and fights follow the year: busy autumns, hard winters.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_WhatYouSow: The peoples remember more; kindness brings visitors and friends, cruelty thins the roads.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_OldPowers: The world feels watched: pilgrims and seers on the road, the land and sky stir, word of strange skies.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_LeanYears: Fewer traders and camps; the region's word turns to famine, drought and hard winters.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_RiseAndFall: Arcs of two years: busy good years, then the region's word turns dark, then the rebuilding.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_StoryDirection_Crossroads: More traders, camps, visitors, favours and debts; some raids come from rivals with a grudge.
